title: The Unwritten Regiment
premise: In the winter of 1899, widowed lighthouse keeper Xanthe Montrose rescues a half-drowned stranger, Elias Wren, who carries letters in the unmistakable handwriting of her late husband's brother — a man officially dead for six years. The letters reveal that Thomas faked his death to escape a regimental scandal and is now alive, hiding among coastal smugglers, while a government historian arrives to seal the official record before the century turns. Xanthe must choose between protecting Elias, whom she comes to love, and forcing the truth into the record by testifying at the year-end inquiry. She testifies, losing Elias to the sea on the crossing but winning Thomas's name back — and discovers in his final letter that he had already written her a place in history.
about_author: August Quintana is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing naval inquiry records along the Cornish coast. Their novels are known for excavating the quiet lives buried inside official paperwork.

chapters.title: The Light Keeps Its Own Hours
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. During the great storms of 1899, she keeps the lighthouse alone, rationing grief as carefully as oil. A wreck washes a stranger, Elias Wren, onto her rocks clutching a waterproof satchel of letters — one bearing her dead brother-in-law Thomas's handwriting. The emotional beat: guarded loneliness cracking open with the first shock of the impossible.

chapters.title: A Corpse Corresponds
chapters.summary: Alternating Xanthe and Elias POVs. Elias confesses he was Thomas's courier, smuggling letters between the 'dead' man and a handful of believers; now someone is hunting the correspondence. A government historian, Mr. Calloway, arrives at the village asking pointed questions about the Montrose family. The beat: complicity deepening into trust, and trust shading toward love neither will name.

chapters.title: The Inquiry at Year's End
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, with an interlude from Thomas's hidden journal. Calloway offers Xanthe silence in exchange for the letters; refusing means ruin, accepting means erasing Thomas forever. She learns Elias plans to flee alone to spare her. The climax: she chooses testimony over safety, taking the boat through the last storm to reach the inquiry before midnight on December 31st.

chapters.title: Entered Into Record
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She testifies; the record is amended, though the victors' historians soften it within a generation. Elias is lost to the crossing, but among his effects she finds Thomas's final letter — addressed to her, insisting her keeping of the light was itself worth recording. The resolution: belonging found not in rescue or romance, but in what she writes down and keeps burning.
